title: Reverse a Linked List

concept.title: A list is nodes that point to the next node
body: A **singly linked list** is a chain of **nodes**. Every node holds a value (`val`) and a reference to the next node (`next`); the last node points to nothing (`None`, `nullptr` or `null`). You hold only the **head**, the first node, and reach everything else by following `next`.
In these problems the starter code already builds the list from the input for you (the `ListNode` type, `build_list` and `print_list` are given). You only write the function that works on the nodes.

To **reverse** a list, walk along it and turn every `next` pointer around. You need three references: the node you are at (`head`), the node before it (`prev`, which becomes its new `next`), and the next node, saved **before** you overwrite the pointer, otherwise the rest of the list is lost.

body.code:
prev = None
while head is not None:
    nxt = head.next      # save the rest of the list
    head.next = prev     # turn the pointer around
    prev = head          # move both references one step
    head = nxt
return prev              # the old tail is the new head

body: No new nodes are created: only pointers change, so the work is O(n) time and O(1) memory.

statement: Reverse a singly linked list and print its values from the new head to the new tail.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of nodes. The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail.
outputFormat: Print the values of the reversed list on one line.
hints: Walk along the list once and change every `next` pointer.
Before you change `head.next`, save it in another variable.
Keep a reference `prev` to the node you came from; at the end it is the new head.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))


def reverse_list(head):
    # Your code here
    return head

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_list(reverse_list(build_list(a)))
free_nodes()

explanation: Each step saves the next node, points the current node to the previous one, and moves on. At the end `prev` is the old tail, which is the new head.
